title: Large Language Models Persuade Without Planning Theory of Mind
abstract: arXiv:2602.17045v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: A growing body of work attempts to evaluate the theory of mind (ToM) abilities of humans and large language models (LLMs) using static, non-interactive question-and-answer benchmarks. However, theoretical work in the field suggests that first-personal interaction is a crucial part of ToM and that such predictive, spectatorial tasks may fail to evaluate it. We address this gap with a novel ToM task that requires an agent to persuade a target to choose one of three policy proposals by strategically revealing information. Success depends on a persuader's sensitivity to a given target's knowledge states (what the target knows about the policies) and motivational states (how much the target values different outcomes). We varied whether these states were Revealed to persuaders or Hidden, in which case persuaders had to inquire about or infer them. In Experiment 1, participants persuaded a bot programmed to make only rational inferences. LL

translated_title: 大型语言模型在无规划心智理论的情况下进行说服
translated_abstract: 摘要：越来越多的研究尝试使用静态、非交互式的问答基准来评估人类和大型语言模型（LLMs）的心智理论（ToM）能力。然而，该领域的理论工作表明，第一人称互动是ToM的关键组成部分，而这类预测性、旁观式的任务可能无法有效评估这一能力。我们通过一项新颖的ToM任务来弥补这一差距，该任务要求智能体通过策略性地揭示信息，说服目标选择三个政策提案之一。成功取决于说服者对特定目标的知识状态（目标对政策的了解程度）和动机状态（目标对不同结果的重视程度）的敏感性。我们变化了这些状态是对说服者“揭示”还是“隐藏”，在隐藏情况下，说服者必须询问或推断这些状态。在实验1中，参与者说服一个仅进行理性推断的机器人。
tldr: 本文提出一种新颖的互动式心智理论任务，发现大型语言模型在说服中无需规划心智理论即可成功，挑战了静态基准评估的有效性。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces a novel interactive theory-of-mind task, revealing that large language models can persuade without planning theory of mind, challenging the validity of static benchmarks.
